title: Placebo control: a victim with no member among the candidates yields no unsupported claim

invariants.description: The decoy victim's training set contains none of the candidates: the record must carry the placebo contract with 0 actual members (0/500), so membership AUC, TPR and the membership-leakage test are undefined rather than computed from placebo labels.

Neither attack may separate placebo group A (victim-training pool, not trained on) from group B (evaluation pool) (observed no claim; 0/20 seeds label known, 2/20 label unknown — within chance at alpha 0.05).
Threshold-attack placebo AUC must stay near chance (observed 0.498; 20-seed range 0.462–0.542). Same bound as the v1 invariant, now on the correctly named metric.
Shadow-attack placebo AUC must stay near chance (observed 0.505; 20-seed range 0.451–0.544).
Call-rate difference between the two placebo groups must stay near 0 (observed 0.000; 20-seed range −0.080 to +0.080).
NEW (defined on real non-members): at the threshold calibrated for 1% FPR, at most 3% of the 500 actual non-members may be called members (observed 4/500 = 0.8%; 20-seed max 2.2%).
The decoy victim is as overfit as the real one (observed gap 0.298), so the null result is due to non-membership, not to a weaker model.

rationale: A placebo, not a membership evaluation: the same pipeline, candidates and attacks against a victim whose training set contains none of them. Until schema v1 this case scored the designated groups as if they were members and non-members; under schema v2 membership metrics use actual membership (undefined here) and the group comparison is reported as placebo population discrimination. A placebo claim would reveal a population difference or a pipeline leak. The genuine low-leakage reference with real members is MLB-REG-026.
